## Scope

The organizational governance artifacts — templates, RACIs, registers, and
a signed SCRM charter — that close nine NIST PM-family controls for
FedRAMP 20x. Thesis: **PM controls are the organizational preconditions
that contextualize all technical evidence**; without them (especially
PM-30), the Book 15 SBOM pipeline is "a technical experiment rather than a
governance artifact."

## Learning objectives

- Draft an Information Security Program Plan (ISPP) covering
  purpose/scope, legal authority, objectives, and budget per
  PM-1/PM-7/PM-11.
- Construct a security leadership RACI assigning AO, CISO, ISSO,
  DevSecOps, SOC, and Privacy roles across ATO, POA&M, incident response,
  and BOD 26-04 activities.
- Implement the three-layer system inventory (Azure Resource Graph, SBOM,
  Entra ID) with monthly reconciliation.
- Apply the NIST SP 800-39 three-tier risk framework and the 5×5
  likelihood-impact matrix with its escalation thresholds.
- Build a testing/training/monitoring plan mapped to KSI themes.
- Draft a PM-30 SCRM Governance Charter with the five NIST SP 800-161r1
  risk categories and supplier requirements.
- Maintain a PM-15 security contact registry (CISA, FedRAMP PMO, MS-ISAC,
  MSRC).

## Key concepts

- ISPP fillable template with FISMA/A-130/EO 14028 authority citations;
  named-individual requirement for AO/CISO.
- Three-layer inventory: Resource Graph export, Syft SBOM manifest, Entra
  identity plane.
- Risk scoring: Score = Likelihood × Impact; 1–4 accept, 5–9 90-day
  POA&M, 10–15 30-day, 16–25 AO escalation in 15 days.
- SCRM organizational chart and the five supplier requirements (SBOM in
  30 days, PSIRT/24h contact, 72h incident notice, VEX in 30 days, audit
  rights).
- Application lifecycle gates: Concept → Design → Build → Deploy →
  Operate.

## Artifact sequence

Artifact-shaped rather than phase-dated: why PM controls gate
authorization → ISPP + EA integration → leadership RACI → inventory
framework → risk management strategy → T&T&M plan → contact registry →
SCRM charter with signature block.

## Compliance hooks

PM-1, PM-2, PM-5, PM-7, PM-9, PM-11, PM-14, PM-15, PM-30 (9 controls);
references SR-2/3/5/6/8/10/11, SA-10, SA-11, AC-21, CM-8(1), CP-4,
FIPS 199. FedRAMP 20x: KSI-SCR (KSI-015, KSI-016), KSI-003, and the
per-theme monitoring dimensions.

## Prerequisites

Book 15 (the SBOM pipeline is PM-30's technical backbone); references
Books 06, 08, 09, 10, 11 per its integration appendix.

## Labs

1. Complete the ISPP and RACI templates for a fictional system, replacing
   all fillable fields with named roles.
2. Write the Azure Resource Graph inventory query and reconcile its output
   against a sample SBOM manifest, logging discrepancies as POA&M items.
3. Score five sample risks on the 5×5 matrix and assign responses and
   POA&M deadlines per the thresholds.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- Technical evidence without PM artifacts "cannot be contextualized" —
  governance is not optional paperwork.
- Inventory discrepancies unresolved within 30 days become POA&M items;
  reconciliation must actually run monthly.
- Risk acceptance above score 4 must be time-bounded with AO concurrence.
- The SCRM charter is only PM-30 evidence when signed, dated, and
  version-controlled with supersession notes.
